summary: Plan audit found 5 blocker/major finding(s) before authoring.

replanFindings.subject: SC-09
replanFindings.message: The plan assigns the model-provider credential to the playground mediator, but the existing runtime exclusively loads and consumes that credential. Satisfying the wording would require forbidden runtime/provider-proxy work or use of the private server package from the public-surface-only playground.

evidence.detail: apps/server/src/config.ts validates OPENAI_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY and apps/server/src/container.ts passes those keys directly to ProviderRegistry factories.
WS-48 requires apps/playground to consume only @swiftagent/sdk/react public surfaces and forbids runtime or SDK additions.
ProviderConfig supports baseUrl, but buildContainer exposes no server configuration that routes provider traffic through a playground mediator.

replanFindings.subject: SC-10
replanFindings.message: The workstream that publishes the built-and-verified scaffold claim does not depend on the workstream that builds and verifies the scaffold.

evidence.detail: WS-49 owns the SC-10 documentation pass and depends only on WS-47 and WS-48; WS-46 is absent.
README.md and docs/vision.md currently mark create-swift-agent Planned, and packages/create-swift-agent does not exist.

replanFindings.subject: SC-11
replanFindings.message: The unqualified ban on every active private publishing posture contradicts nine intentionally private existing workspace packages. The intended domain must be stated as the three public packages and their public-consumer path.

evidence.detail: pnpm-workspace.yaml expands to private manifests for @swiftagent/api, db, gateway, models, observability, runtime, server, example-backend, and example-frontend.
AGENTS.md and WS-44 both intend non-publishable packages to remain private.

replanFindings.subject: SC-05
replanFindings.message: WS-45 permits a tarball-backed substitute even though SC-06 requires publishing the CLI into a registry and resolving it through npx. A directory of tarballs or file dependencies is not an npm registry endpoint.

evidence.detail: WS-45 includes 'Verdaccio-backed (or tarball-backed) local registry'; WS-46 requires publishing create-swift-agent into that registry and exercising real npx resolution.

replanFindings.subject: SC-15
replanFindings.message: The plan treats a version tag as immutable without defining any GHCR enforcement. Compose should pin the manifest-list digest so the multi-architecture image reference cannot drift.

evidence.detail: WS-50 accepts an 'immutable version tag or digest', while GitHub's package lifecycle permits container package versions to be removed/replaced and no immutable-tag policy is specified.
A sha256 manifest-list digest is produced after the multi-arch push and directly satisfies SC-15.

evidence.detail: WS-51 is the graph root; no final workstream explicitly owns the repeated four-command proof after apps/playground and packages/create-swift-agent are added.

criticSummary: SC-09: The mandated mediator cannot literally own the provider credential in the existing architecture. apps/server/src/config.ts reads provider keys, apps/server/src/container.ts constructs the model providers inside the runtime, and the provider registry supplies them directly to the runtime loop. The playground backend is separately constrained to public SDK use and is described as sitting between the browser and that runtime. Moving the credential into the mediator would therefore require a provider-proxy/runtime configuration feature or embedding the private server package, both excluded as runtime/public-surface work. The limit and ledger portions are otherwise expressible: RunRecord exposes terminal tokenUsage through GET /v1/runs/:runId, and an app-specific mediator protocol can define refusal frames without adding ChatEvent variants.; SC-10: WS-49 owns the documentation change that declares create-swift-agent built and locally verified, but WS-49 depends only on WS-47 and WS-48. WS-46, which actually builds and verifies the scaffold, is on a separate tail and is not a dependency. The orchestrator can therefore execute and green WS-49 while the claimed artifact does not exist. README.md and docs/vision.md currently both say the scaffold is planned, so this is a real ordering defect rather than an already-reconciled disposition.; SC-11: The literal rule 'No ACTIVE repository surface still asserts or enforces a private/restricted publishing posture' conflicts with the canonical workspace roster: @swiftagent/api, db, gateway, models, observability, runtime, server, example-backend, and example-frontend are intentionally private and must remain so. The enumerated surface set clearly intends only the three public packages and their consumer path, but that qualifier is absent from both criterion copies. For the intended three-package domain, the twelve grouped surfaces are complete: a repository-wide active-file search found no additional private-registry assertion.
